title: Harbison Parts-and-Labor Protection: Original Claim Decision and Its Posting Tool
content:
**What this covers.** The original decision on a claim filed against a Harbison 10-Year Parts & Labor Protection, Harbison 12-Year Total Protection or Harbison 12-Year Total Protection Plus contract — the parts-and-labor tiers of Harbison Protection Contracts — and the approved amount written on that decision. The coverage tests of the claim rules decide whether the claim is approved at all; a claim whose part the manufacturer supplies is partially approved for the parts; and the decision is made on the filing date. The claim decided is the claim filed on the contract on the date of handling, together with the service call, failed unit, failed component and failure date recorded on it.

**What the posting does.** The decision is posted as the claim's original decision: one decision entry, decision round 1, on the contract's claim history, dated the day it is posted, carrying the outcome, the governing reason for any refused part and the approved amount. The entry does not change the contract's remaining claim benefit or the service invoice. The holder and the agent can see the decision in the claim history right away.

### Tool: `decide_parts_labor_claim_22401446`

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, passing the parameters below.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `contract_id` | reference number of the protection contract the claim was filed against, from the protection contract lookup | id |
| `claim_id` | reference number of the claim being decided — the claim-file entry's own reference number, from the contract's claim history | id |
| `ticket_id` | reference number of the service call on which the failure was diagnosed and repaired, from the claim-file entry or the service call lookup | id |
| `equipment_id` | reference number of the failed unit named on the claim, from the claim-file entry or the equipment lookup | id |
| `install_id` | reference number of the Harbison installation of the covered equipment, from the protection contract; echoed on the receipt | id |
| `decision` | the outcome of the decision | one value of the enum below |
| `denial_reason` | the governing reason for a denial or for the refused part of a partial approval | one value of the enum below |
| `approved_amount` | the amount approved on the decision | US dollars, 2 decimal places, positive, rounded to the cent half up; 0.00 on a denial |

`decision` takes exactly one of: `approved` (every tested part of the claim passes and the claim is paid as decided); `partially_approved` (part of the claim is refused, as when the manufacturer supplies the part, and the rest is paid); `denied` (the claim fails a coverage test and nothing is paid).

`denial_reason` takes exactly one of: `none` (approved with nothing refused); `component_not_covered` (the failed component is not covered by the tier); `outside_coverage_term` (the failure date is outside the coverage dates); `maintenance_not_documented` (documented maintenance is not current); `filed_after_deadline` (filed after the filing deadline); `waiting_period_not_elapsed` (the failure came before coverage started after a waiting period); `manufacturer_parts_coverage_applies` (the manufacturer's parts warranty supplies the part); `limit_exhausted` (no claim benefit remains); `excluded_cause` (the failure stems from an excluded cause); `contract_not_active` (the contract was not active).

**Return.** A receipt listing `claim_entry_id` (reference number of the decision entry just posted), `claim_id`, `contract_id`, `ticket_id`, `install_id`, `decision`, `denial_reason` (empty when none), `decision_round` (always 1), `approved_amount` (US dollars, 2 decimals) and `entry_date` (today). The presence of `claim_entry_id` means the decision is on record.
